title: Smart routing: progressive failover (percentage-based routing) w/ staged rollback + metrics
author: Elena Popov
description:
Context: As part of the Regional failover automation upgrade (ENG-2846), we need the routing layer to support progressive failover so the orchestrator can shift traffic in controlled increments (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and roll back quickly without rewriting policies by hand. This PR adds percentage-based routing ("progressive failover") to policy evaluation, plus rollback support and core metrics for visibility. This is gated behind a feature flag and defaults to no-op when the progressive policy fields are not present.

What’s included: Adds a new optional routing policy override section to express progressive failover per scope (customer tier, route, model) using weights between primary region and target region. Implements deterministic request bucketing so the same customer/request key stays stable across evaluations (reduces thrash during partial steps). Adds rollback primitives: (1) explicit rollback target weight, (2) step-down behavior with max decrement per interval, and (3) a "freeze" mode where orchestrator can hold weights while investigating. Emits metrics for the evaluated progressive state + routing decision, with tags for region, target_region, tier, route_id, and policy_revision (careful: tier/route_id are low-cardinality; model_id is hashed to avoid runaway cardinality).

Key design points: Request selection is stable via rendezvous hashing over (tenant_id, route_id, normalized_model_family, request_bucket_salt). We store the chosen bucket in the request context so retries don’t re-roll the dice. Weight evaluation is done in the policy layer, not in the edge, so Dedicated + Hosted share the same behavior. Rollback is a first-class operation: orchestrator can drop weights in controlled steps and we record a reason code in the evaluation result (e.g., "rollback_operator", "rollback_safety_guard").

Safety/guardrails in this PR: Hard clamp of weights to [0,100]. Enforce that primary+target == 100 in the progressive section (reject config otherwise). Add a max_step_delta_per_minute (default 50) to prevent accidental full cutover in one update when using automation. Feature flag: routing.progressive_failover.enabled (off by default in prod). This PR does not include capacity gating / safe-to-failover checks (tracked in ENG-2845 / PR 98305).

Observability: New counters and histograms: routing_progressive_failover_evaluations_total{decision=primary|target|bypass, reason=*}; routing_progressive_failover_weight{scope=*} gauge (exported from policy snapshot); routing_region_decision_total{source=progressive_failover|baseline}; routing_policy_validation_errors_total. Adds trace annotations on the routing span: progressive.failover.enabled, progressive.failover.weight_target, progressive.failover.reason.

Testing: Adds unit tests for bucket stability, distribution sanity (approx within 1% over 100k keys), config validation, and rollback step-down logic. Adds an integration test that applies a policy revision sequence 0%->10%->25%->0% and asserts monotonic behavior + no request-context rerolling.

Rollout plan: Land behind feature flag. Staging will enable for a single internal route with canary weight=5% during the next game day. Production enablement will be a low-risk slice (internal/low-tier) with monitoring on new metrics + existing regional SLO dashboards.

Notes for reviewers: Please pay attention to (a) policy validation + error handling path (we should fail closed to baseline routing), (b) metric cardinality, and (c) deterministic bucketing key choice. Mina asked to keep the policy surface area minimal; this is currently one optional object under routingOverrides.

Follow-ups: Add UI exposure in Console to show progressive weights in routing debug view (Felix/Chloe). Wire orchestrator to use the new policy fields and record audit events (PR 98248/98277 pairing).
commits: routing/eval: deterministic bucketing + weighted region selection
routing/context: persist progressive bucket key across retries
telemetry: progressive failover metrics + trace annotations
tests: unit + integration coverage for weight transitions and rollback
docs: internal comments + config examples for orchestrator integration
checks: Build (bazel) — pass; Unit tests — pass; Integration tests — pass; Lint/format — pass; Typecheck — pass; SAST (semgrep) — pass. Initial CI run failed once due to a flaky distribution test threshold; rerun after adjusting tolerance and seeding passed.
conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): The overall approach looks right, but I’m worried about policy validation behavior. If the progressive object is present but invalid, do we reject the whole policy or just ignore progressive fields? Please fail closed to baseline routing and emit a validation metric (we cannot have routing blow up because someone fat-fingered 101%). Also, can you confirm request bucketing does not include raw model_id to avoid cardinality issues? Elena Popov (author): Agree. Updated validation to treat progressive section as optional; invalid progressive override is ignored with a policy_validation_errors_total increment + debug log including policy_revision. Also swapped model_id for normalized_model_family + hashed model for trace tag only.

Vikram Singh (review): For rollback, please ensure we can step down in increments. I don’t want an operator to type 0 and instantly shift everything back if DNS/edge changes are still propagating. Is max_step_delta_per_minute enforced in the eval layer or just validation? Elena Popov (author): Enforced in eval layer using last_applied_weight from the policy snapshot (persisted with revision). If delta exceeds clamp, we clamp and mark reason=clamped_step_delta. Added integration tests.

Benji Okafor (review): Feature flag is good. Please add an explicit bypass path when flag disabled (no extra CPU work), and a counter for bypass decisions so we can confirm the flag is actually off. Elena Popov (author): Done. Early return before hashing when disabled; added decision=bypass metric.

Allison Grant (review): Metric tags look mostly safe, but route_id can still be high. Are we sure route_id is bounded? Could we tag route_group instead? Elena Popov (author): For now route_id is already used in routing metrics and is bounded by customer configs; still, I changed the default emitted tag to route_group and kept route_id behind a debug config (routing.metrics.include_route_id=false by default). Also added model tag hashing.

Peter Holtz (review): I want to confirm the selection is stable across retries and streaming reconnect. Where does the bucket live? Elena Popov (author): Stored in request context (header propagation inside the mesh) as x-rw-route-bucket. Retries reuse it; if absent, we compute. Added tests and docs in code comments.

Mina Haddad (approval): Looks good after changes. Please make sure orchestrator team knows about the clamp reason codes; they should display them in audit logs. Approved.

Merge: Squashed and merged after CI green + approvals. Release note not required (internal, flagged).
release_notes: Internal: adds progressive failover support in smart routing behind feature flag routing.progressive_failover.enabled. No customer-facing behavior change unless enabled.
